title: How to polish locomotion?
author: chmillout
selftext:
Hey everyone, I noticed that creating quick cool prototypes with almost any model is pretty easy and mindblowingly fast but polishing is a nightmare. Any tips how to improve the smoothness of animations, blending, logics?

I’ve experimenting with different LLMs to create this “advanced locomotion” for around a month already and still can’t get it smooth enough, still all kinds of random glitches appear here and there and it is so frustrating to explain what to fix to Claude or Devin or Codex. They fix one thing but break another in a never ending loop. It’s like these 10% that are left to finally get the locomotion just right are the hardest.

Do you have any pipelines or prompts or advices how to make LLMs plan out the animation speeds, blendings, smoothness and for example make sure the hands grab exactly ledges and not the air for the ledge grabs? You can see that legs and hands are constantly clipping through surfaces. 

You can test this prototype on itch - https://chmillout.itch.io/aeonsparadise

It’s mobile friendly so you can play from your smartphone in portrait mode.

Any kinds of advices would be appreciated greatly!

P.S. Yes I did use Astra but it burns all my credits in 5 minutes and doesn’t even ends a task, it’s ridiculous.

comments.author: lorendroll
comments.body:
* **Fix foot sliding** by matching the player's animation playback speed to their actual velocity. Measure the character's movement distance during a single animation cycle based on foot-ground contact, or estimate it visually, then adjust the animation speed to match the capsule's movement speed.
* **Implement a Blend Tree** for strafing and diagonal movement (45 deg. angles) to ensure smooth transitions between movement vectors. Align the timings and keyframes of these animations so they blend seamlessly.
* **Apply inertialization** for animation transitions instead of traditional crossfading to preserve bone velocity and momentum as a post-process step.
* **Smooth out directional changes** by blending into a strafe before turning 90 degrees. As the character's facing direction rotates smoothly, layer in a leaning animation to reflect weight transfer.

replies.author: robobax
replies.body: All of this, plus adding a lean in to player movement direction, is going to make a huge improvement in visibility and feel.

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
1 have your ai update documentation after every change it makes 

Have your ai also create a test suite 
So that after changes it runs the test suit to see if something else might be breaking 


I use opencode but documentation. MD files is very important 

Claude code quality sucked for me and I don't support openai that stole work from open-source projects 

But documentation remains important to any ai , it's a way for it to quickly fetch context without needing to go and constantly read the entire project

replies.author: Brave-History-6502
replies.body:
I find that too much documentation can burn tokens and end up confusing agents. Like a ball and chain eventually. 

I think that is why Boris cherny recently recommended once in a while removing Claude.md and checking how it impacts performance.

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
Rule sets , project index ,   having orchestration info to set up agents 
Project end goal 

Those are all supposed to be separate documents 

Orchestration reads most 
And sub agents only gets access to what it needs to work on 

That doesn't burn more tokens 
Repeating the same prompts and fixing constant repeated bugs is a burn of tokens

comments.author: PatchyWhiskers
comments.body: I think most people here use manual editing of models for final polish, AI is not pro-quality in 3D yet, due to limited training data.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
it looks quite decent to me already. if AI already had a few passes at it, I doubt that it can further polish the animations.

probably just need to manually make the adjustments yourself at that point. it doesn't take a lot of learning to manipulate bones and change keyframes.
